{{Quote|Stay out of this, Tenel Ka. You can't possibly know anything about it. You have the emotional depth of a ronto.|[[Jaina Solo Fel|Jaina Solo]]|<ref name="The New Jedi Order: Star by Star">''[[The New Jedi Order: Star by Star]]''</ref>}}
'''Ronto''' were large, quadruped [[Mammal/Legends|mammals]] that were commonly used as beasts of burden by the [[Jawa/Legends|Jawas]] of [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]]. They were known for their loyalty and strength, being able to carry hundreds of kilograms of weight. They were large enough to frighten off [[Tusken Raider/Legends|Tusken Raiders]], though they were easily spooked by machines, such as [[Speeder bike/Legends|speeder bikes]]. They were commonly used on [[Nubia/Legends|Nubia]] and [[Benja-Rihn]].

==Characteristics==
{{Quote|You're growing faster than a ronto!|[[Dama Whitesun Brunk]], to young [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]]|<ref name="A New Hope: The Life of Luke Skywalker">''[[A New Hope: The Life of Luke Skywalker]]''</ref>}}
[[File:Ronto.jpg|thumb|left|150px|A ronto with its handler, stomping a landspeeder]]
Like the native [[Dewback/Legends|dewbacks]] of [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]], ronto were easy to train and became quite fond of their masters,<ref name="TEGtAS">[[The Essential Guide to Alien Species (real-world book)|''The Essential Guide to Alien Species'']]</ref> whose faces they associated with food.<ref name="Invincible">''[[Legacy of the Force: Invincible]]''</ref> Rontos had superb senses of hearing and smell, although they had poor vision, which is why they were startled by sudden movements. Rontos needed large amounts of [[Water/Legends|water]],<ref name=":0" /> although their skins shed excess heat, allowing them to function well in desert conditions. They were rarely exported, though, because offworlders thought their skittishness made them unreliable in urban areas. Another reason the ronto was popular with the Jawas is that Jawas did not usually visit urban areas, so it was ideal for desert travel.

When in heat, [[Gender/Legends|female]] rontos gave off a powerful, musky scent much like the smell of a [[Rodian/Legends|Rodian]]. During mating season, Rodians on Tatooine were encouraged to stay away from male rontos, lest they inadvertently become the target of a ronto's affections.

Rontos could hear sounds in the range of 32 kHz.<ref name="DV3D">''[[Star Wars: Darth Vader: A 3-D Reconstruction Log]]''</ref>

Rontos were extremely loyal and easily domesticated. They developed deep bonds with their masters and their keen sense of smell serveed as an early warning to riders of imminent dangers. Their size was such that only the largest of [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]]'s predators risk attacking them. Even [[Tusken Raider/Legends|Sand People]] kept their distance from rontos, though a hungry [[Krayt dragon/Legends|krayt dragon]] feared little from the gentle herbivore.<ref name=":0" />

==Related species==
A species that appeared to be related to the ronto lived on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Kashyyyk/Legends|Kashyyyk]]. In contrast to their Tatooine cousins, they had a darker coloration, a more elongated cranium, and much smaller [[Ear/Legends|ears]]. They also appeared to be less easily spooked than their cousins and were in fact quite aggressive if they came under attack. While typically encountered in small groups, how they came to the planet is unknown.

==Behind the scenes==
The rontos added into the [[Mos Eisley/Legends|Mos Eisley]] scenes for the [[The Star Wars Trilogy Special Edition|Special Edition]] release of ''[[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|A New Hope]]'' are entirely computer-generated. The ronto used brachiosaur digital models crafted for ''Jurassic Park'' as a starting point with enough modification to make it distinctly ''[[Star Wars]]''. Throughout the making of the sequence, the [[Industrial Light & Magic|ILM]] animators referred to the otherwise nameless creature as a "bronto." When asked to name the animal, [[George Lucas]] dropped the 'b' from the name, and thus the ronto was christened.<ref name=":0">{{DB|creature|ronto|ronto}}</ref>
